## About {#about}

::: {.intro-grid}
::: {}
### Phylogenies

A phylogeny is a [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetic_tree) or [network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetic_network) that describes the history of a group of organisms, populations, species, or languages. A node can represent a splitting event, such as population divergence or speciation, or a merging event caused by hybridization, [introgression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Introgression), [gene flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_flow), or [admixture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_admixture).
:::

::: {}
### Research uses

Research in evolutionary biology uses [phylogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetics) and [phylogenomics](https://hal.science/hal-02535070v3/) to infer phylogenies from molecular sequence data. Researchers use those phylogenies to study [trait evolution](https://lukejharmon.github.io/pcm/), diversification, and other evolutionary patterns.
:::
:::
:::

## Packages {#packages}

JuliaPhylo contributors build packages for phylogenetic analysis. Many rely on the core PhyloNetworks package. The [Julia phylogenetics task view](task-view.qmd) also lists related software by use case.

::: {.featured-package}
::: {.featured-package-heading}
<img src="assets/PhyloNetworksLogo.png" class="package-logo" alt="PhyloNetworks logo">

### [PhyloNetworks](https://github.com/JuliaPhylo/PhyloNetworks.jl/tree/master)
:::

PhyloNetworks provides tools for reading, writing, analyzing, and manipulating phylogenetic trees and networks. It supports extended Newick, quartet concordance factors, distance and dissimilarity measures, network summaries, and inference through parsimony and neighbor joining. Its traversal and network manipulation functions also support specialized packages.
:::

::: {.package-grid}
::: {.package-card}
<img src="assets/snaq-logo.png" class="package-logo" alt="SNaQ logo">

### [SNaQ](https://github.com/JuliaPhylo/SNaQ.jl)

Infer level-1 phylogenetic networks from quartet concordance factors using maximum pseudolikelihood and a heuristic search of network space.
:::

::: {.package-card}
### [PhyloTraits](https://github.com/JuliaPhylo/PhyloTraits.jl)

Simulate and analyze continuous and discrete trait evolution along phylogenetic trees and networks. Fit models, estimate ancestral states and rates, and study correlations between traits.
:::

::: {.package-card}
### [PhyloCoalSimulations](https://github.com/JuliaPhylo/PhyloCoalSimulations.jl)

Simulate phylogenies under the network multispecies coalescent, including models with inheritance correlation.
:::

::: {.package-card}
### [PhyloPlots](https://github.com/JuliaPhylo/PhyloPlots.jl)

Plot tree and network objects from PhyloNetworks through R via RCall.
:::

::: {.package-card}
### [Quarnet GoF](https://github.com/JuliaPhylo/QuartetNetworkGoodnessFit.jl)

Measure the goodness of fit of a phylogenetic network to data on four-taxon subsets.
:::

::: {.package-card}
### [PhyloGaussianBeliefProp](https://github.com/JuliaPhylo/PhyloGaussianBeliefProp.jl)

Analyze Gaussian models on phylogenetic networks and admixture graphs using belief propagation.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.home-section .resources-section}
## Resources {#resources}

These repositories and tutorials complement the JuliaPhylo packages.

- [PhyloUtilities](https://github.com/JuliaPhylo/PhyloUtilities) provides scripts and [pipeline documentation](https://juliaphylo.github.io/PhyloUtilities/) for phylogenetic analyses.
- The [comparative methods tutorial](https://juliaphylo.github.io/networkPCM-tutorial/) covers reticulate phylogenies and network calibration. An [earlier workshop](https://cecileane.github.io/networkPCM-workshop/) covers PhyloNetworks 0.16.
- The [SNaQ tutorial](https://solislemuslab.github.io/snaq-tutorial/) covers network estimation from quartet concordance factors.
- The [TICR repository](https://github.com/nstenz/TICR) provides scripts for analyzing genome-wide data, obtaining quartet concordance factors, and assessing tree-like evolution.
:::
